### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8c5ebc764aece48d8239b405c6fb537b2b690ecd` — the merge of head `46c4246f66c0528d68c74ad9a8446190e4bf0ce6` into base `d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8c5ebc764aece48d8239b405c6fb537b2b690ecd && git checkout 8c5ebc764aece48d8239b405c6fb537b2b690ecd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a 46c4246f66c0528d68c74ad9a8446190e4bf0ce6 && git checkout -B drift-repro d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a && git merge --no-ff 46c4246f66c0528d68c74ad9a8446190e4bf0ce6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d08b859a7177cf16d6190163f2e42efa2d980d3a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `46c4246f66c0528d68c74ad9a8446190e4bf0ce6`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration — `record-recognisers.mjs --paths <9 changed paths>` derives no schema, rules or narrowing face; the committed changeset `.changeset/28715-mcp-validate-expression-label-targets.md` carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, so the review owed is the declaration face alone (`--face declaration` ⇒ `TIER_DEFAULT`). Reviewed the diff of head `46c4246f` against merge-base `7a48bf73` (on `origin/main`), the card (#28715: triage 6559838316, claim 6561442620, os-dev-report 6562313371), the order, the PR body and the head's check-runs. No ④ on this face.

Read at 2026-11-01T18:56Z; the head is pinned above.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **One judge, same code and sentence (order ruling 1).** CORRECT. `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` keeps the single `validateExpression(role, expression, hint)` call and only adds `optionFields` to `hint` (`...(optionFields ? { optionFields } : {})`). The refusal is the validator's own `checkOptionLabelTargets` (`packages/formula/src/validate.ts`), code `label-field-no-options`, sentence `optionlessLabelSentence(field)` (`packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts`), the one the door's lint pass (`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`, formula-field `expression`, `optionFields: optionFieldNames`) surfaces as `expression-invalid`. The tool returns `result.errors` unprojected, so code, `params.field` and message are byte-identical to the door's. No second spelling of "declares options": both bridges import `declaresOptions` from `@objectstack/formula`. An object with declared fields and no option-bearing field answers `[]`, which is truthy and still hands the check its (empty) set — the same verdict the door gives on that body.
2. **Predicate matches the document each bridge reads (order ruling 2).** CORRECT. Stdio: `optionFieldsOf` reads `objectView.getObject(name)` — the very read `describeObject` makes (`stdioObjectView`: `readMergedObjects` via `protocol.getMetaItems({ type: 'object' })`, else `metadataService.getObject`). HTTP: `describeObject` and `optionFieldsOf` now share one `readServedObject(name)` (merged `readMergedItems(protocol, 'object')`, else `meta.getObject`), so the two cannot read different objects. Both documents are served bodies: the registry's `finishServedObject` → `resolvePicklistFields` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `resolvePicklistFieldsOnto`) writes a picklist-bound field's resolved `options` beside `picklist`, and the boot bridge copies `registry.getAllObjects()` — that served body — into the metadata service (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `metadataService.register('object', …)`), which is why the dev's probe read resolved options on the fallback too. So `declaresOptions` (served form) is the matching predicate, and the picklist-bound `tier` reads ok on both bridges (pinned: stdio `['kind','stage','tier']` in `mcp-validate-expression.option-labels.test.ts`; HTTP both read paths in `mcp-option-fields-read.test.ts`). I found no bridge path that serves the AUTHORED form on a kernel that runs ObjectQL. Residual, not a must-fix: a host with a metadata service but no registry (no `ObjectQLPlugin`) would hold authored bodies and `declaresOptions` would refuse a picklist-bound `label()` there; such a host evaluates no formula and is not a measured MCP deployment. Noted under ③.
3. **Site gate (order: parity with lint per site).** CORRECT. Lint hands `optionFields` on exactly one `validateExpression` call, the formula field's `expression` (`validate-expressions.ts` ~3231); the `validation` predicate call (~2384), the flow-condition call (~2480) and the `template` calls (~2874, ~3751) hand none. `VALIDATE_SITE_MAP` marks `formula` alone `optionLabels: true`, and the handler asks the bridge only then; the site control pins `validation`/`flow_condition`/`template` deep-equal to a bridge without the member, and the second ablation (ask on every site) reds that control. `main` has moved `validate-expressions.ts` since the merge-base (b3572509b, flow message slots); that commit touches no `optionFields`/`declaresOptions` line, so the per-site reading above holds on the landing base.
4. **The new optional bridge member.** CORRECT and additive. `optionFieldsOf?(name): Promise<readonly string[] | null>` is optional on `McpDataBridge`, read behind `bridge.optionFieldsOf` so an implementer that omits it gets no `label()` target check (the validator's opt-in: `optionFields` absent ⇒ check does not run) — pinned by the "bridge without optionFieldsOf answers as before" control. `McpDataBridge` is re-exported from `packages/mcp/src/index.ts` and the package `exports` map addresses `./dist/index.*`, so the member lands on the published accept set: the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration (deviating from the claim's expected `no`) is the right reading, and the PR body says so. `describe_object` is unchanged: neither bridge's projection (`name`/`type`/`label`/`required` per field; `name`/`label`/`fields`/`enableFeatures`) gains a key; the HTTP `describeObject` hunk is a pure factor-out into `readServedObject`; pinned on both bridges. Census pins (`BRIDGE_MEMBERS`, `RECIPES`) classify the member as reading no row body and writing no record — right, it reads field names off the object definition only.
5. **Unknown field / other sites unchanged.** CORRECT. `checkOptionLabelTargets` judges only names in `schema.fields`, so `label(record.nope)` keeps exactly `['unknown-field']` (pinned). Non-`record` sites are untouched (see 3).
6. **Controls, ablations, parity, red-first.** Present and sound. Red-first on base sources: mcp 4/13 red (bridge member, both LIT, PARITY), runtime 2/2 red (`optionFieldsOf is not a function`). Ablation 1 (drop `optionFields` from the hint) reds the two LIT cases and PARITY only, every control green — the order's predicted shape. Ablation 2 (ask on every site) reds the site control only. PARITY drives the same object through `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` (authored body, picklist-bound `tier` with no `options`) and through `validate_expression` (served body) for five expressions: same verdict, same error count, door message contains tool message. The order's parity hypothesis is met on the stdio transport; the HTTP bridge is pinned on the same served shape through the real `/mcp` entry (`HttpDispatcher.handleMcp`), and a real-kernel round trip through both transports is declared out of this PR. `packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts` gains the `@objectstack/formula` source alias that `check:test-source-alias` prescribes for the new import; the alias is anchored and scoped to the bare specifier.
7. **Overlap.** At 2026-11-01T18:56Z, by REST, the open PRs on `packages/mcp/src/` are #28774 itself and #28772; only #28772 (draft, head `79470662`, internal-field evaluation refusal) touches `stdio-data-bridge.ts`, in the import block (~133–160), a new helper (~548) and the `query`/`aggregate` arms (~954, ~1077). #28774's hunks are the `declaresOptions` import after line 127 and `optionFieldsOf` between `describeObject` and `query` (~945–958): different lines, no semantic overlap. Whichever lands second rebases textually at most.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/mcp: patch`, `@objectstack/runtime: patch`, beside `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset. CONSISTENT: under ruling A (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, "the level follows the protocol": `none` ⇒ every introduced entry `patch`) and AGENTS.md §3 ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`"). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right — nothing an author can write is added, refused or re-read; the door already refused this formula (#28714). The head's `Check Changeset` run concluded `success`. The widening is a TypeScript-only optional member; no tool input or output shape moves, so no wire consumer is affected.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Author:** PR `user.login` = `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay login to name.
- **Claim deviation (dev flag):** claim expected `Clause-②: no`; measured `yes (widening)`. ANSWERED in ① 4: correct, and this record is the review the order said the seat would run for a widening.
- **`open_questions`:** none declared.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` (dev, carrier none, not filed):** Studio's live CEL lint (`celAuthoring.ts`) is another face of the same judge that cannot see field options. ACCEPTED as out of scope here: it is a client surface outside `packages/mcp`, unmeasured, and no finding of this review depends on it. Not escalated; the seat may file a p3 card from the dev's note when it measures.
- **Reviewer's residual (not a must-fix):** `declaresOptions` on a host whose metadata service holds AUTHORED bodies (no `ObjectQLPlugin`, so no boot-bridge served copy) would refuse a picklist-bound `label()` through MCP where the door accepts it. No measured MCP deployment has that shape (the MCP data tools need the engine), and the order ruled the predicate by the document measured on real kernels. Recorded so a future host without the registry knows which reading to re-measure.
- **CI at 2026-11-01T18:56Z:** 45 check-runs on head `46c4246f`; 0 red; 16 still `in_progress` (Build Core, Test Core 1–8, Type Check ×3, Lint ×4). Every completed required-family run is `success` (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, PR Size, Auto Label, Lint · PM dispatch-gates). Landing precondition ② (all green) is the seat's to re-read before enqueue; this record does not wait on it.
- **Local gate claim:** the dev's `28715-gates-ran.txt` records 60 derived families exit 0 on this head; read, not re-run.
